assumptions._rule: Five-year hold, exit at the entry multiple (no multiple expansion), debt sized off EBITDA and held fixed in pounds while the entry price moves, all spare cash repays debt.
assumptions._cash: Where a filing has a cash flow statement, capex uses the actual figure and the working-capital drag is 1 minus cash conversion (capped at 30%, never below 0).

multiple_ranges._rule: Range applied to latest-year EBITDA. Recurring-type businesses (revenue visibility estimate 0.6 or more) use the services range; project-based businesses use the contractor range. Small EBITDA (under the threshold) takes a size discount.

recurring_services.why: Gamma (UK business communications, 89% recurring revenue) traded near 6x before its bid and was taken private at about 7.6x; Crowe puts listed UK services at 7.5x. Our companies are far smaller, so the range sits at or below these.

project_contractors.why: SPIE, a large listed technical services group, trades near 8x; UK private deals under £250m have a median near 6x. Project-by-project revenue and small size put these at a discount to SPIE.

network_asset_owners.why: Owners of towers and fibre networks are priced by infrastructure funds, well above services firms: VodafoneZiggo's Dutch towers sold at 16.2x 2025 EBITDA (DigitalBridge-led consortium, 2026) and Bite's TeleTower at 16x EBITDAaL (Stonepeak). UK fibre deals are often priced per home and include distressed sales, so the range starts lower.
